vakbeschrijving.nl:
Central to this course is data collection in the French regional parc of the ‘Baronnies Provençales’ (in the Drôme Region). In teams of three, you will prepare, execute, and report on an Application-Driven Project based on a Field Survey. In short, you are given a ~50km2 area in the southeast of France for you and your team to do fieldwork so that you collect – bottom to top – scientific data to solve a scientific and/or engineering problem.

Before the field work, there will be two weeks of preparation in Delft. During these weeks, your time will be dedicated to equipping you with solid field-based workflows to characterise the geosphere (geology), the atmosphere (atmosphere observations) and everything in between (hydrosphere and biosphere; Remote sensing). In the second preparation week, you will also get training for a specific Application-Driven Project (ADP).  The outcome of this second preparation week is the plan of your field campaign that combines field-based technologies, methods, and workflows. 

During field work (weeks 4.6, 4.7, and 4.8), you start with general field activities, which we call the ‘Field Survey’ and aim at having you characterising the Earth’s spheres with a focus on the geosphere. You do that by following the scientific method. In all phases of your field work, you will be acquiring Earth and Climate data daily, in a systematic manner. 

There, for about one third of your time, you will be conducting specific field activities for your ADP. The “FIELD survey” from your area will feed data to your selected “application-driven PROJECT”, together making your FIELD PROJECT unique. With additional field methods and technologies, you will be able to work on a real problem with your data.

Once you are back to Delft and for two weeks, you will report on your team’s findings about your area and ADP in an oral presentation.

Students with disabilities who cannot participate in the field work would join a team and assist them either from Delft or the field camp.

Field Project = Field Survey + Application-Driven Project (ADP)

leerdoelen.nl:
After taking this course, you will be able to:

Design a manageable field survey plan that combines field-based technologies, methods, and workflows aimed at solving an application-driven project. ILO5, ILO10 

Execute field-based workflows to efficiently and systematically acquire Earth and Climate data in the field in a quality-controlled manner to characterize the Earth’s spheres and their interactions, while following scientific, health, safety, and environmental standards. ILO4, ILO5, ILO10, ILO11

Interpret Earth and Climate data acquired by you, your team, and neighboring teams you share areas with, as an interconnected puzzle of the Earth’s spheres. ILO2, ILO4, ILO10, ILO13

Construct deliverables (e.g., time series, maps, cross-sections, logs, etc...) that characterize, quantify, and visualize Earth’s spheres using Earth and Climate field data as well as open-access data.  ILO2, ILO10, ILO11

Evaluate the quality of the deliverables constructed with data from a field study area using suitable methods, metrics, and validation data, and discuss quality, sources of error, and uncertainties associated with field measurements. ILO10, ILO11, ILO13

Reflect critically and independently on the interpretation of your field data and results and that of other teams, to inform and adjust your team’s decisions, in all phases of a field project. ILO13

Manage a Field Project with your team from its initiation to its conclusion, through constructive peer feedback and appropriate presentation techniques. ILO5, ILO10, ILO11

toelichting_onderwijsmethode.nl:
Pre-Field Project (First semester and early second semester) 

Logistics: Make teams, book your accommodation, get an area attributed to your team, and arrange for your transportation to – and in – the field work area.   

Preparation phase (2 weeks; 2x40 hours of total time) 

Lectures: Fieldwork Introduction & HSE, available Application-Driven Projects, Sampling method and bias, 

Practical: Geological workflow, GIS/Remote Sensing workflow, Atmospheric workflow, Field reconnaissance, Dunham classification, Geological mapping, and VRock sessions.

Training: Drone training, specific to the ADP (methods & technologies), and HSE Training.

Assignments and deliverables (see details in Assessment forms and moments and weekly descriptions): First through third sets of deliverables. 

  Field work phase (3 weeks; 3x40 hours of total time) 

First Day: 

  • Excursion to familiarize students with geologic, remote sensing, and atmospheric observations.  

Field Activities : 

  • Geology: 1) Find outcrops, 2) characterize outcrops (i.e., surveying of the geosphere from the surface) by gathering data, samples, and following a checklist (e.g., location, dip angle/azimuth, grain size, geomorphologic feature, layering and alternations, structural features, etc...) associating a quality flag/weight to each collected data, 3) Interpret outcrops: based on collected information, make an educated guess about the stratigraphy, sedimentology, and structural geology, 4) test hypothesis by going towards predicted younger or older strata in the stratigraphic series, and 5) repeat while completing the field outcrop (fact) and geological (interpretation) maps. Keep detailed notes in a field notebook.  

  • Remote Sensing: 1) Identify different type of land surface components (i.e., surveying of the biosphere, geosphere and hydrosphere from the surface and the atmosphere), 2) classify the land surface by gathering data, samples relating to soil type / vegetation species, geometric and spectral characteristics (including height and surface temperature), coverage and distribution, 3) obtain waypoints and 4) repeat  

  • Atmospheric Observations: Students measure micro-meteorological (i.e., surveying of the atmosphere from the surface) variables (e.g., air temperature, humidity, windspeed, precipitation) both at a centralized and mobile location and observe cloudiness every day (individual fixed location near their starting point). 

  • Application-Driven Project (ADP): field activities will depend on the selected project and will be detailed with the projects offered each year (list of available ADP projects is subject to change each year).  

Camp activities: 

  • Geology: draw structural, outcrop, and geological maps; construct cross sections; write detailed description of outcrops, catalog/archive collected rock samples (sedimentology), encountered rock formations (stratigraphy), and major folds/faults (structural geology); tidy up and back up field notebook; plan geology survey for next day; liaise with neighboring teams.   

  • Remote Sensing: Maintaining a GIS project, collecting training data, and making land cover map.  

  • Atmospheric Observations: review daily weather in comparison to forecast and look at and take note of the forecast for the following day. 

  • ADP: camp activities will depend on the selected ADP and will be detailed with the projects offered (list of available ADP projects is subject to change each year).  

Activities for team gatherings (once a week, at your discretion or may be supervised, with 2-3 teams with overlapping areas): 

  • Geology: compare geological maps and cross-sections, plan joined field days, share collected field data, and discuss implications of discrepancies; 

  • Remote Sensing: compare classification method and results, discuss implications of discrepancies  

  • Atmospheric Observations: look at the whole dataset, analyzing means, medians, standard deviations and discussing patterns (diurnal cycle), outliers and/or comparison against climatology, uncertainties and problems with the sensors, based on their initial measurements, students test a hypothesis regarding the impact of surface coverage on the observed temperature, design a measurement strategy (e.g., measurements synchronized with a different team, etc...) and test their hypothesis (also in light of other local and larger-scale factors, such as incoming cold fronts or changing cloud cover) 

Field survey assessment activities (end of the second week):  

  • Four assessed discussions (pass/fail) of 20min each, over your deliverables for the following disciplines: Stratigraphy and sedimentology; Structural Geology; Remote Sensing; and Atmospheric observations.  

  • One final discussion of 20min to go over your plans for your ADP in the following week, with oral formative feedback from the responsible instructor.  

Assignments and deliverables (see details in Brightspace): Fourth through sixth sets of deliverables (Check-out). 

 Reporting phase (up to 2 weeks; up to 80 hours of total time) 

Oral presentation: You and your team prepare the presentation of your Field Project with a focus on the field ADP.  Instructors will have ‘walk-in’ moments when you can ask them questions in the week following fieldwork.  A rubric is available in Brightspace. Your team presentation will take place at the start of the second week. If a resit is needed, that will be organized on the last day of the second week. 

Portfolio: An executive summary of your ADP is required for your portfolio at the end of the reporting phase.  

Assignments and deliverables (see details in Brightspace): Seventh set of deliverables.
